A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the BCPs act through two distinct mechanisms: (1) the stimulation of adenylate cyclic activity by beta-BCP(7-37), and (2) a temperature-sensitive mechanism that may involve the activation of a Gi-like protein by alpha-BCP and gamma-BCp.
the bag cell peptides are able to modulate adenylate cyclases in a manner consistent both with their physiological effects and with the effects they have on cAMP levels when added to intact cells.
the BCPs act through Gs and/or Gi to alter cAMP levels in the bag cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bag cell peptides are not just a set of tools for studying bag cell physiology, but are also useful in studying adenylate cyclases and G-proteins.
the BCPs are not simply modulators of bag cell activity; they also have a direct, temperature-dependent effect on adenylate cyclases, and this effect is mediated by Gs and/or Gi.
the BCPs are capable of modulating adenylate cyclases directly.
